spec_match.rationale: Implements the spec's stated motivation — labelling the inside and outside of a closed shape without duplicating or reversing path data — with side="right" on the single path, against the genuine hand-reversed-duplicate baseline.

interactive.rationale: The implementation toggle swaps the inside label between the reversed-duplicate path and side="right" on the original, with a measured aria-live verdict and side-by-side markup diff.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises the old hack running beside side="right" with a markup diff; the page delivers both, measured.

edge_cases.rationale: The unsupported tier is shown as the real broken rendering (both labels outside, overlapping) with the readback explaining it and pointing back to the working mode — the honest failure is itself the migration argument.

references.rationale: chromestatus entry, spec section and MDN linked.

conformance.rationale: The suite's closed-path movement, default-left and invalid-value assertions pin exactly the contracts this page relies on.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP, both modes: reversed-duplicate measured waterInside=true landInside=false (the old way genuinely labels both sides here), side mode measured both outside with the readback calling it the wrong side; console clean; mobile emulation overflow-free. A baseline-position measuring bug was caught in screenshot review and replaced with glyph-box-centre measurement before ship. The equivalence claim (side mode identical to hack) still needs a supporting engine and is the open question.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the probe, the reversed-duplicate-recommended fallback branch, and each mode switch with measured inside/outside flags.

design_system.rationale: Variables only; lake stroke uses --accent-blue on --bg-stone fill, labels are --accent-blue / --text-charcoal on ivory, diff blocks scroll horizontally inside their own pre elements.

accessibility.rationale: role=img SVG with title, fieldset/legend radios at 44px with visible focus, aria-live measured verdict describing which label sits where.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360x740 DPR3: zero horizontal overflow, diff columns stack, no console errors.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive demo control panel sliders without horizontal overflow on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Long code blocks belong in their own horizontal scroll containers on narrow screens (css / css-layout).
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both markup-diff pre blocks have overflow-x auto and the diff grid collapses to one column below ~560px; 360px emulation shows zero page overflow.
The aria-live verdict reports measured inside/outside for both labels after every toggle, including the honest wrong-side report on unsupported browsers.

openQuestions.title: Prove the equivalence claim on a supporting engine
openQuestions.detail: The page argues side="right" renders identically to the hand-reversed duplicate. On Chrome 156 or Firefox, toggle both modes and compare the measured water-label positions (they should match within a pixel); consider asserting that equivalence in the page when both modes are measurable.

summary: The practical migration: one shoreline labelled on both sides, with the working hand-reversed-duplicate hack measured against side="right" on the single path, and the markup diff showing what the attribute deletes. Chromium 141 evidence confirms the hack works and shows the side-mode's wrong-side rendering honestly.
